claim.statement: Measures the digest-checked executables named in products, launched with the lock's fixed launch. For an official target each release tag's commit is attributed source context only: nothing ties an executable to it, so no built-from, equivalence or same-build claim is made. Mailpit, MailHog, MailSlurper, smtp4dev and Inbucket are official artifacts, and MailSlurper's official release executable does not start with its default SQLite storage (a CGO_ENABLED=0 build; a published result, so that row is blocked and carries no number); the mailslurper-source-build row is a different executable, MailSlurper release-1.15.0 built from source with cgo on a host glibc (unpinned runtime), not an official artifact, and both MailSlurper executables report v1.14.1 under tag release-1.15.0; GreenMail is an official jar bound to its Maven Central artifact by the registry's own checksum (integrity against that checksum; authenticity not verified), run on a pinned JRE; the alkemio-mailslurper row is a third-party patched image's extracted binary, run natively on the musl loader pinned from the image's own layer and never counted as an official competitor row, and the swarmail candidate is neither. MailSlurper, smtp4dev and Inbucket tag their releases lightweight, which carries weaker source evidence than an annotated tag. Throughput and observed visibility within the declared deadline are all that is claimed: no durability, no accept==stored and no equivalence. Storage is the unmatched profile and resources the unenforced local profile; both are stated in every report. Targets without a verified server search are scanned completely and filtered on the client, and GreenMail is read over POP3; both are labelled per row.
